System description:
# Case: Uber ATG automated test vehicle (Tempe, Arizona, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-19/03. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A modified Volvo XC90 SUV is used by Uber Advanced Technologies Group (ATG) to test an automated driving system (ADS) on public roads. The ADS is designed to drive the vehicle without human input in defined conditions, up to about 45 mph in this test program.

## Main parts
- Sensors: roof-mounted lidar, radar units and cameras covering the area around the vehicle.
- Perception: detects objects around the vehicle, classifies each one (for example vehicle, pedestrian, bicycle, other), and tracks it over time.
- Prediction: estimates where each tracked object will go next, using its class and recent movement.
- Planning and control: chooses a path and speed, and controls steering, throttle and braking.
- Vehicle: the Volvo factory driver-assistance features (such as forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking) are part of the base vehicle.

## People
- One vehicle operator sits in the driver seat. The operator is responsible for watching the road and taking over control when needed. The operator also uses a tablet-style interface to tag events and check system status.
- Other road users share the road: pedestrians, cyclists and other drivers. They are not aware of the test program.

## Operating context
Public multi-lane roads in an urban area, day and night, with posted speed limits, marked crosswalks, intersections and street lighting that varies by location.

goals.text: Conduct ADS testing on public roads.
Drive the vehicle without human input in defined conditions.
Operate within the test program speed limit of about 45 mph.
Observe the area around the vehicle using lidar, radar, and cameras.
Detect objects around the vehicle.
Classify detected objects, such as vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles.
Track detected objects over time.
Estimate where tracked objects will go next using their class and recent movement.
Choose a path and speed for the vehicle.
Control the vehicle's steering, throttle, and braking.
Provide the factory forward collision warning feature.
Provide the factory automatic emergency braking feature.
Watch the road and monitor vehicle operation.
Take over control when needed.
Tag events using the tablet-style interface.
Check system status using the tablet-style interface.
Travel safely as a pedestrian on roads shared with the test vehicle.
Travel safely as a cyclist on roads shared with the test vehicle.
Operate a vehicle safely on roads shared with the test vehicle.
Share the road safely with other road users.

requirements.text: The system shall, in each validated operating scenario where a pedestrian is within the defined safety-relevant area, either maintain a pedestrian detection and track or treat the area as potentially occupied and slow or stop before entering it; validation shall include partial occlusion, unusual pedestrian positions, and the specified lighting range.

The planning system shall treat every low-confidence detection in the vehicle’s path as a potential hazard and select a speed and path that permit stopping before the detection’s conflict area until it is resolved as non-hazardous.

The system shall monitor operator readiness and issue a takeover request with enough lead time for the defined operator response time and vehicle stopping distance; if readiness is lost or the request is not acknowledged within the specified time, the ADS shall perform a controlled stop.

The prediction and planning systems shall account for plausible sudden entry of a pedestrian into the vehicle’s path, including entry from between parked vehicles or outside a crosswalk, and shall limit speed so the vehicle can stop before the resulting conflict area.

The perception system shall report classification confidence and shall not use an uncertain or changing pedestrian-or-cyclist classification as the sole basis for prediction or planning; until resolved, downstream systems shall handle the object as a vulnerable road user.

When a tracked road user is occluded or sensor visibility changes, the tracking system shall preserve an uncertainty region for that user and the ADS shall treat that region as occupied until the user is reacquired or the region is confirmed clear.

The system shall detect when sensor degradation or unavailability reduces coverage below the defined minimum, and shall restrict operation or perform a controlled stop before proceeding into an area that cannot be adequately observed.

For every hazard the ADS is required to respond to, the control system shall initiate braking no later than the point at which the vehicle’s measured speed, braking capability, and available distance require braking to stop before the defined conflict area.

The system shall measure actual vehicle speed independently of the commanded speed and prevent actual speed from exceeding the configured test-program limit, including by reducing propulsion or braking when needed.

The ADS shall compare monitored conditions with explicit, testable operating limits and shall not continue automated driving when any required condition is outside those limits; it shall transition to a controlled stop or other defined safe state.
